subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

items.prompt: List the levels of organization from smallest to largest: cells, organs, tissues, organ systems.

steps: Cells build tissues, tissues build organs, organs build systems.

items.prompt: What is a group of similar cells working together called?

steps: Similar cells grouped together form a tissue.

items.prompt: What forms when different tissues work together as a unit (like the heart)?

steps: Different tissues combine to form an organ.

items.prompt: Which system breaks food into nutrients the body can use?

steps: The digestive system breaks down food into nutrients.

items.prompt: Which system carries nutrients and oxygen to the body's cells?

steps: Blood in the circulatory system delivers nutrients and oxygen.

items.prompt: Which system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide?

steps: The lungs of the respiratory system exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

items.prompt: Explain why body systems are called subsystems.
items.answer: Because each one performs part of the work of the whole-body system

steps: Each system is a smaller part of the larger body system.

items.prompt: Describe one way the respiratory and circulatory systems work together.
items.answer: The respiratory system takes in oxygen and the circulatory system carries it to cells

steps: Oxygen enters at the lungs and the blood distributes it.

items.prompt: Why can no single organ system keep the body alive on its own?
items.answer: Because the systems depend on one another and must interact to meet the body's needs

steps: The systems cooperate; each relies on the others.

items.prompt: A runner's muscles need more oxygen and nutrients. Name two systems that respond together.
items.answer: The respiratory and circulatory systems (and the digestive system supplies nutrients)

steps: Breathing increases and blood flow increases to meet the demand.

items.prompt: What is the smallest level of organization listed: cells, tissues, organs?

steps: Cells are the smallest of these levels.

items.prompt: The stomach is made of several tissues. What level of organization is it?

steps: Different tissues forming a unit make an organ.

items.prompt: Which system removes carbon dioxide from the body?
Why must the digestive and circulatory systems interact?
items.answer: Digestion releases nutrients that circulation must deliver to cells

steps: The systems depend on each other.

items.prompt: Name the level of organization between tissue and organ system.

steps: Tissues form organs, which form organ systems.
